title: CyberChef installer comparison with an explicit resource list

methodology.execution: Separate fresh Node processes, retained baseline completed before retained explicit-list run started.
methodology.applicationExecution: None. The baseline optional worker script returned HTTP404, so no installer Worker was constructed; the new installer downloads/parses resources only.
methodology.environment: Node on this development machine; no browser and no CORS simulation. Browser-origin CORS checks are separate evidence.
methodology.instrumentation: Native global fetch wrapped to record requested URL, response status, credentials mode and request-header completion timing. Whole installation measured with performance.now(). Output resource byte counts and SHA256 are installer output, which may include adapted documents/scripts.
limitations: One elapsed-time comparison, not a statistical benchmark or pure CPU measurement.
The runs use live network resources and different resource graphs; explicit installation captured more resources and bytes.
Module import and initial source hashing occur before the timed installation.
No shared cache was installed by the harness. Network/server/CDN cache state is uncontrolled.
A preliminary overlapping trial was discarded; only the subsequent sequential pair is retained.
Each installer synthesizes four inline-script resource URLs with random identifiers. Those output URL differences are adaptation artifacts; the request trace records actual network URLs.
methodology.sourceIntegrity: Every TypeScript source file was hashed before and after each run; both retained runs had stable source hashes. The new source is a dirty implementation worktree, so HEAD alone is not its implementation identity.
